# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 76 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 76 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_076_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 76 contains one of the most theologically dense passages in Hermas: the identification of the virgins as "holy spirits" who are the "Powers of the Son of God," and the claim that the Son of God himself bears the names of these virgins (76:3). This is a unique early Christian pneumatology in which virtues are hypostatized as divine Powers associated with the Son.

The "seal" (*sphragis*) in 76:1 refers to baptism — the baptismal seal. Those who receive the name (Christ) at baptism but do not receive the virgins' garment (i.e., the virtues) cannot enter the tower. The name-without-garment is useless: "you will bear his name in vain" (*matēn phereis to onoma autou*, 76:2).

The phrase "Powers of the Son of God" (*dynameis tou Hyiou tou Theou*) interprets the virgins as divine attributes that constitute the Son's spiritual presence in the believer. This is not abstract virtue ethics but a Spirit-christology: to be clothed by the virgins/holy spirits is to be clothed in the Son's own Power.

The rejected stone categories in 76:4-6 cover three fates: (1) stones that rolled off the road into rough terrain — those who believed but became double-minded and abandoned the true path; (2) stones burned in the fire — complete apostates with no thought of repentance; (3) stones near the water — those who heard the gospel and wanted baptism but pulled back when confronted with purity's demands. The third category is particularly poignant — closest to salvation but drawing back.

All three agents agree substantially. Main disagreements involve handling of "it profits you nothing," "clothe him," and the phrase "the names themselves are the garment."

---

## Similitude 9, Part 3 — The Rejected Stones and the Virgins

**76:1** Some stones were brought from the deep and placed in the building, and they joined well with the stones already set in from the plain — for they were very bright. But some of these brought by men did not fit into the building; these were set aside near the tower, because they could not be used in the structure. For they had not received the seal, while the others all had the seal of the virgins.

**76:2** "Who are these virgins?" I asked the shepherd. "They are holy spirits," he said. "And a man cannot enter the kingdom of God in any other way unless these clothe him. For if you receive the name but do not receive the garment from them, it profits you nothing. For these virgins are the Powers of the Son of God. If you bear the name but do not bear his power, you will carry his name in vain."

**76:3** "But the stones that were rejected — who are they?" I said. "These," he said, "are those who bore the name but did not put on the garment of the virgins." "And what is their garment, lord?" I said. "The names themselves are the garment," he said. "Everyone who bears the name of the Son of God ought also to bear the names of these virgins. For the Son of God himself bears the names of these virgins."

**76:4** "But those stones thrown far from the tower that fell onto the road and then rolled off into the rough terrain — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who had believed, but then because of their double-mindedness abandoned the true road. Thinking they could find a better road, they went astray and were afflicted, wandering in the rough places."

**76:5** "And those that fell into the fire and were burned — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who fully apostatized from the living God, and repentance no longer entered their hearts, because of the desires of their licentiousness and the wicked deeds which they committed."

**76:6** "And who are those that fell near the waters and could not roll into the water?" "These," he said, "are those who heard the word and wished to be baptized in the name of the Lord. But then, when the purity of the truth came to their memory, they drew back and went off again after their evil desires."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
